```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## 1. Aim

This document reads the UNDP Gender Inequality Index (GII), joins it to a
world countries spatial dataset, and calculates the change in gender
inequality between 2010 and 2019.

A **negative** difference means inequality fell (improved) between 2010 and
2019. A **positive** difference means inequality rose.

## 2. Packages

```{r packages}
library(sf)          # read and handle spatial data
library(tidyverse)   # data wrangling (dplyr, readr, ...)
library(here)        # build file paths relative to the project
library(janitor)     # clean column names
library(countrycode) # convert country codes (ISO2 -> ISO3)
library(tmap)        # quick maps
```

## 3. Data

Two files are stored in the `data/` folder of this project:

* **Gender inequality data**: "All composite indices and components time
  series (1990-2023)" CSV from the UNDP Human Development Reports data centre
  (<https://hdr.undp.org/data-center/documentation-and-downloads>).
* **World countries**: a `.geojson` of country boundaries (e.g. *World
  Countries (Generalized)* from ArcGIS Hub, or the file provided on Moodle).

> Change the file names below if yours are different.

```{r read-data}
# Gender inequality data (CSV). latin1 keeps names like "Côte d'Ivoire" readable.
hdr <- read_csv(here("data", "HDR25_Composite_indices_complete_time_series.csv"),
                locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"),
                na = c("", "NA", ".."))

# World spatial data (GeoJSON)
world <- st_read(here("data", "World_Countries_Generalized.geojson"))
```

Check what the data look like before joining:

```{r inspect}
# Column names of the spatial data
names(world)

# Gender inequality columns all start with "gii_"
hdr %>%
  select(iso3, country, starts_with("gii_")) %>%
  head()
```

## 4. Wrangle the gender inequality data

Keep only the columns we need and calculate the difference.

```{r wrangle}
gii <- hdr %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  # keep country rows only (regional aggregates have iso3 starting with "ZZ")
  filter(!str_starts(iso3, "ZZ")) %>%
  select(iso3, undp_country = country, gii_2010, gii_2019) %>%
  mutate(gii_diff_2010_2019 = gii_2019 - gii_2010)

head(gii)
```

## 5. Join to the spatial data

The world GeoJSON uses **2-letter** ISO codes (column `ISO`), while the UNDP
data uses **3-letter** ISO codes (`iso3`). We use `countrycode` to create a
matching 3-letter code before joining.

```{r join}
world_gii <- world %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  mutate(iso3 = countrycode(iso, origin = "iso2c", destination = "iso3c")) %>%
  left_join(gii, by = "iso3")

# How many countries did not get a match?
sum(is.na(world_gii$gii_diff_2010_2019))
```

> Some countries have no GII value for 2010 or 2019, and some territories
> (e.g. small islands) are not in the UNDP data, so a few `NA` values are
> expected.

## 6. Results

Countries where gender inequality fell the most, and where it rose:

```{r table}
world_gii %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(gii_diff_2010_2019)) %>%
  arrange(gii_diff_2010_2019) %>%
  select(undp_country, iso3, gii_2010, gii_2019, gii_diff_2010_2019) %>%
  head(10)
```

```{r map, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
tmap_mode("plot")

tm_shape(world_gii) +
  tm_polygons("gii_diff_2010_2019",
              palette = "-RdBu",   # blue = inequality fell, red = rose
              midpoint = 0,
              title = "Change in GII\n(2019 - 2010)",
              textNA = "No data") +
  tm_layout(main.title = "Change in Gender Inequality Index, 2010-2019",
            legend.outside = TRUE)
```

## 7. Save the output

```{r save}
dir.create(here("output"), showWarnings = FALSE)
st_write(world_gii, here("output", "world_gii_2010_2019.gpkg"),
         delete_dsn = TRUE)
```

## 8. Reproducibility

The raw data are not pushed to GitHub (see `.gitignore`). To reproduce this
analysis, download the two files listed in Section 3 into a `data/` folder
and knit this document.
